cohort: 8,508,228 women with nonanomalous singletons, without diabetes or hypertensive disorders, and delivered at 36 to 41 weeks, from the U.S. vital statistics datasets from 2011 to 2013
finding: Women with cerclage who delivered at 36 to 41 weeks had significantly higher rates of composite maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes, chorioamnionitis, and cesarean delivery compared to those without cerclage.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were significantly higher in women with cerclage compared to those without.
